label: Google Workspace
setupConsole: Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials
setupSteps: Create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID (type: Web application).
Add the redirect URI shown below to 'Authorized redirect URIs' on YOUR client.
Enable the Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Sheets, Docs, Slides, and Tasks APIs for the project.
Choose admin-consent (domain-wide) vs per-user consent on the OAuth consent screen.
Paste the Client ID + Client secret below; we validate by dry-running the consent URL.
scopesRationale: gmail.modify/calendar/drive/spreadsheets/tasks back the Google Workspace skills; openid+email identify the account.

label: Dropbox
setupSteps: Create an app: Scoped access, Full Dropbox access.
On the app's OAuth 2 section, add the redirect URI shown below.
On the Permissions tab, enable account_info.read, files.metadata.read, files.content.read, files.content.write, sharing.read, sharing.write — then Submit.
Paste the App key (Client ID) + App secret (Client secret) below.
scopesRationale: files.content/metadata read+write back browse/download/upload; sharing.read/write let the agent manage shared links; account_info.read identifies the account.

label: GitHub
setupConsole: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps (or GitHub App)
setupSteps: Register a new OAuth App (or a GitHub App for installation tokens).
Set the Authorization callback URL to the redirect URI shown below.
Select the repo/org scopes the agent needs.
Paste the Client ID + Client secret below.
scopesRationale: repo/read:org back the GitHub skills (PRs, issues, org-visible repos) as the connecting user.

label: X (Twitter)
setupConsole: X Developer Portal → Projects & Apps → your app → User authentication settings
setupSteps: Set up User authentication: OAuth 2.0, type Confidential client, App permissions Read and write.
Add the Callback URI shown below to the app's Callback URLs.
Under Keys and tokens, generate the OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret.
Paste the Client ID + Client secret below.
scopesRationale: tweet.read/users.read back reads; tweet.write lets the connecting user post as themselves; offline.access issues a refresh token so the 2-hour access token renews.

label: Zoom
setupConsole: Zoom App Marketplace → Develop → Build App → General app
setupSteps: Create a General app and choose User-managed. Until it is published, only users in your Zoom account can connect it.
Add the redirect URI shown below as the OAuth redirect URL and to the OAuth allow list, with strict mode on.
Under Scopes, add meeting:read:meeting, meeting:read:list_meetings, meeting:write:meeting, meeting:update:meeting, meeting:delete:meeting, and user:read:user.
Paste the Client ID + Client secret below — the Development credentials unless the app is published.
scopesRationale: Zoom grants the scopes configured on the app rather than a requested list; the meeting scopes let the agent find, create, reschedule, and cancel meetings the connecting user hosts or schedules, and user:read:user reads their Zoom profile and timezone.
